subject: ela
intro: When you describe someone, a place, a thing, or an event, you use relevant details to help your listener picture exactly what you are talking about. Relevant details are specific facts or observations that directly relate to the topic. Good descriptions include: sensory details (what you see, hear, smell, taste, or touch), specific adjectives, and clear feelings. Weak descriptions are too vague — they use words like 'nice,' 'good,' or 'fun' without saying WHY or HOW.

items.prompt: A student wants to describe her dog. She says: 'My dog is nice.' Is this a good description? What could she say instead?

steps: 'Nice' is vague — it does not tell the listener anything specific.
A better description uses specific details: color, size, behavior, sound.
Better: 'My dog is a small golden retriever with fluffy fur. She wags her tail and runs to me every time I come home.'
solution.answer: 'My dog is nice' is too vague. A better description: 'My dog is a small golden retriever with fluffy fur. She wags her tail and always runs to greet me.'

items.prompt: A student describes a birthday party: 'We had cake. It was great.' What specific details could make this description better?

steps: Add sensory details: what did the cake look like? taste like?
Add specific events: what games were played? who was there?
Add feelings: how did the student feel?
Better: 'We had a chocolate cake with blue frosting and rainbow sprinkles. I blew out all eight candles in one breath, and everyone cheered. I felt so happy!'
solution.answer: Better: 'We had a chocolate cake with blue frosting. I blew out all eight candles and everyone cheered. I felt so happy!' — this uses sensory and specific details.

items.prompt:
Which description of a thunderstorm is better?
A) 'The storm was scary.'
B) 'The thunder boomed so loudly the windows shook. The lightning flashed bright white across the dark sky. I pulled my blanket up to my chin.'

steps: Option A is a single vague word ('scary') — does not paint a picture.
Option B uses sensory details: sound (thunder boomed), sight (lightning flashed white), touch (pulled blanket up).
Option B also shows the feeling (pulling blanket up shows fear) rather than just labeling it.
solution.answer: B) is better. It uses specific sensory details and actions that show the experience, not just label it.

items.prompt: What does it mean for a detail to be 'relevant'? Give an example of a relevant and a non-relevant detail when describing a fire truck.

steps: A relevant detail directly relates to the subject being described.
Relevant detail about a fire truck: 'It is bright red with a long ladder on top and a very loud siren.'
Non-relevant detail: 'My uncle once ate a sandwich near a fire station.' — this is about the uncle, not the fire truck.
solution.answer: Relevant: directly describes the fire truck (color, ladder, siren). Non-relevant: introduces unconnected information.

items.prompt: A student describes a new classmate: 'She has long brown hair that she wears in two braids. She sits in the front row and always raises her hand first. She smiles when the teacher calls on her.' What makes this a good description?

steps: It includes physical details: long brown hair, two braids.
It includes behavioral details: sits in front row, raises hand first.
It includes an expressive detail: smiles when called on.
All details are specific and relevant — they help the listener picture this person.
solution.answer: It is a good description because it uses specific, relevant physical, behavioral, and expressive details that help the listener form a clear picture.

items.prompt:
Which description of a playground is better?
A) 'The playground was fun.'
B) 'The playground had a tall red slide, two swings, and a climbing wall with rainbow handholds. Kids were laughing everywhere.'

steps: Option A: 'fun' is vague. No specific details.
Option B: 'tall red slide,' 'two swings,' 'climbing wall with rainbow handholds,' 'kids laughing' — all specific and relevant.
solution.answer: B) is better. It uses specific details about the equipment and the scene.

items.prompt: Add TWO specific details to this weak description: 'I saw a bird.'
items.hint: Think about the bird's size, color, sound, or behavior.

steps: Original: too vague — we do not know anything about the bird.
Add details: What did it look like? What did it do?
Better: 'I saw a bright red bird with black wings sitting on the fence and singing loudly.'
solution.answer: Better: 'I saw a small bright red bird with black wings. It was singing a loud, pretty song on the fence.'

items.prompt:
A student describes an event: 'I went to a soccer game. My team won.' Which detail is MOST relevant to add?
A) 'The field was made of green grass.'
B) 'I scored the winning goal in the last minute of the game.'
C) 'My neighbor has a dog named Spot.'
items.hint: Relevant details directly connect to the event being described.

steps: Option A is somewhat relevant (it describes the setting) but not the most important.
Option B is highly relevant — it describes a key event in the game (scoring the winning goal) with specific details.
Option C is completely unrelated.
solution.answer: B) is the most relevant detail to add — it describes a specific, exciting event in the game.

items.prompt: Describe your favorite food using at least THREE specific details (taste, texture, appearance, smell, or feeling).
items.hint: Use your five senses — what does it look, smell, taste, feel like?

steps: Example: Favorite food = pizza.
Detail 1 (appearance): 'golden-brown crust with bubbling cheese on top.'
Detail 2 (taste): 'the cheese is salty and the sauce is tangy and sweet at the same time.'
Detail 3 (texture): 'the crust is crispy on the outside but soft and chewy inside.'
solution.answer: Example: 'My favorite food is pizza. It has a golden-brown crispy crust, bubbling cheese on top, and the sauce is sweet and tangy. The first bite is warm and chewy.'

items.prompt:
A student describes a person: 'My grandpa is really old and nice.' What TWO types of details are missing from this description?
A) Sensory details and specific behavioral/personality details
B) The grandpa's age and phone number
items.hint: Think about what makes a description vivid and specific.

steps: 'Really old' is vague (how old? what does he look like?).
'Nice' is vague (what does he do that is nice?).
Missing: sensory details (what he looks like) and specific behavior/personality details (what he does, how he acts).
solution.answer: A) Sensory details and specific behavioral/personality details are missing.
